description: A third-year student with strong theoretical foundations in Python and Java who is pivoting toward Cybersecurity but feels a significant gap in their knowledge regarding C and low-level memory management.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This module on C-language basics is vital for a student with no prior exposure to ensure they can manipulate the low-level data structures used in OS kernels.
nodes.description: Introduction to C syntax, pointers, and memory management basics necessary for systems-level programming.
nodes.title: Systems Programming Foundations: C & Pointers
The Hardware-Software Interface
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with no prior exposure, understanding the interrupt-driven nature of hardware is a necessary bridge before analyzing software OS structures.
nodes.description: Conceptual overview of the hardware-software interface, including registers, CPU cycles, and the role of the BIOS.

nodes.title: Dev Environment: Linux Tooling & Shell Basics
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mastering the compilation process and shell commands provides the prerequisite technical literacy for a student with no prior exposure to start OS development.
nodes.description: Practical guide to the Linux development environment, using GCC for compilation and basic GDB debugging techniques.

nodes.title: OS Services and System Structures
nodes.description: Core OS foundations covering services, system structures, and the critical distinction between kernel and user modes.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node establishes the essential distinction between user and kernel mode, a foundational concept for all subsequent course modules.

nodes.title: Process Abstraction and Lifecycle
nodes.description: Analysis of process lifecycles, states, and the operations required to manage process creation and termination.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This node covers the fundamental process abstraction which is the primary unit of work for the operating system and a key exam topic.

nodes.description: Techniques for process communication, including shared memory models, message passing systems, and socket programming.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Inter-process communication is a required syllabus topic that bridges individual process management with networked and multi-threaded systems.
nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication (IPC) Mechanisms

nodes.description: Introduction to threads, multi-threading models (M:1, 1:1, M:M), and implicit threading libraries like OpenMP.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Threading is essential for modern high-performance software; every student must master threading models for both exams and projects.
nodes.title: Threading Models and Multicore Programming
CPU Scheduling Algorithms & Evaluation
nodes.personalizationRationale: Algorithmic scheduling is a core analytical objective for the course and is tested heavily on the midterm exam.
nodes.description: Detailed study of CPU scheduling criteria and algorithms like Round Robin, Priority Scheduling, and Multi-level Feedback Queues.

nodes.title: Midterm Review: Foundations to Scheduling
nodes.description: Comprehensive review session and practice exam covering Chapters 1 through 5 to prepare for the week-8 midterm.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This mandatory midterm review ensures the student with no prior exposure has solidified their understanding of foundational concepts before the first major exam.

nodes.title: Process Synchronization & Mutex Locks
nodes.personalizationRationale: Synchronization is a high-difficulty core requirement that every student must apply in their multi-threaded programming projects.
nodes.description: Examination of the critical section problem and tools like mutex locks and semaphores to prevent race conditions.

nodes.title: Monitors and Classic Synchronization Problems
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mastering classic problems is required to demonstrate the ability to model and solve complex concurrency issues analytically.
nodes.description: Analysis of monitors and classic synchronization problems including the Dining Philosophers and Readers-Writers problems.
Study of deadlock characterization, prevention strategies, and the Banker's algorithm for deadlock avoidance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Though a smaller block, deadlock theory is a required part of the cumulative final and essential for system reliability analysis.
nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization and Avoidance
Physical Memory & Paging Mechanisms
nodes.description: Foundations of memory management, covering contiguous allocation, paging concepts, and page table structures.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Physical memory management is a prerequisite for understanding how the OS interacts with modern hardware architectures.

nodes.title: Virtual Memory & Page Replacement Algorithms
nodes.description: Exploration of virtual memory, demand paging, and page replacement algorithms like LRU and Optimal.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Virtual memory is a cornerstone of OS design and a critical component of the semester's memory management project.

nodes.title: I/O Systems and Subsystem Performance
nodes.personalizationRationale: Understanding I/O performance and interfaces is a required capstone skill for completing the system-wide perspective of the course.
nodes.description: Overview of I/O hardware, kernel I/O subsystems, and the interface between drivers and the OS kernel.

nodes.personalizationRationale: File system design is the final core module before the cumulative exam, focusing on how data persistence is managed by the OS.
nodes.description: Investigation of file system implementation, directory structures, and allocation methods for persistent storage.
nodes.title: File System Implementation & Storage

nodes.description: Final comprehensive review session covering all course material from Week 1 through 15 in preparation for the cumulative final exam.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The cumulative final review is mandatory for all students to ensure readiness for the exam which constitutes 40% of the grade.
nodes.title: Cumulative Final Course Review
